ann_28.text: This part acts on only 8 of 242 training patients (3%), all of them women whose chest pain is brought on by exercise.
For them it raises the risk sharply (odds about 55 times on average, on the model's odds scale), but the model has little data on this.
In the training data, 7 of these 8 patients had heart disease.
Women have a lower risk than men in the model, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain or the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy.
Chest pain brought on by exercise raises the risk only if the resting ECG is normal.

ann_29.text: This part barely changes the model's predictions (by at most 0.7 percentage points of risk).

ann_30.text: This part acts on 111 of 242 training patients (46%), nearly all of them patients with a flat ST segment at peak exercise.
For them it clearly raises the risk (odds about 1.9 times on average, on the model's odds scale), and 72 of the 111 had heart disease.
Through it, a flat ST segment raises the risk, and even more so if exercise brings on chest pain.
Through it, being a woman and having chest pain brought on by exercise raise the risk, and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG lower it.

ann_31.text: The model gives the biggest increase in risk to patients with more major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy: from 0 to 2 vessels, the odds rise about 76 times on average, on the model's odds scale.
Compared with patients who have no chest pain symptoms, it gives a much lower risk to patients with typical angina or non-anginal chest pain, and a lower risk to patients with atypical angina.
Women get a clearly lower risk than men (odds about 0.05 times those of men, on the model's odds scale).

A flat ST segment at peak exercise, higher cholesterol (193 to 308 mg/dL), more ST depression on exercise (0 to 2.8 mm), a reversible defect on the thallium scan, older age and chest pain brought on by exercise each clearly raise the risk.
A higher maximum heart rate clearly lowers the risk; fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL lowers it slightly and left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG raises it slightly.

For a typical patient (a 56-year-old man with no chest pain symptoms and median test results, predicted risk 23%), the largest changes on the model's odds scale are about ×76 for 2 vessels instead of 0, about ×14 for a flat instead of an upsloping ST segment and about ×0.03 for a woman instead of a man.
The model has little data on a fixed defect on the thallium scan (15 patients, lower risk) and a downsloping ST segment (17 patients, slightly higher risk).
It ignores resting blood pressure.

ann_28.original: Hypothesis: node 665 is a three-way AND gate that fires only for women (sex:0 set) with exercise-induced angina (exang:0 unset, i.e. exang=yes) and no left-ventricular hypertrophy on resting ECG (restecg:2 unset). The restecg:2 chain 2349 -> 2771 never leaves the ReLU linear region on standardized one-hot inputs (2349 in [1.15,3.11], 2771 in [1.99,3.72]), so the gate collapses exactly to relu(1.41 sex:0 - 1.71 exang:0 - 1.18 restecg:2 - 3.39). Evidence (train, n=242): pre-activation max is 2.117, reached only when all three conditions hold; removing any one condition drives it negative (no female: -0.86; no exang: -2.53; LVH present: -0.24). The gate is active on 8/242 rows (3.3%), always at the single value 2.117, and 7 of those 8 are positive cases. Closed form matches the forward pass (check_explanation closed-form err 0.0049, numeric err 0).
ann_28.proposed: A part that sharply raises the risk for the 8 training patients who are women with chest pain brought on by exercise (7 of them had heart disease); in the model, chest pain brought on by exercise raises the risk only if the resting ECG is normal.

ann_29.original: Hypothesis: node 2447 is an always-active affine relay of restecg:2 (LVH on resting ECG). Evidence (train): pre-activation in [0.485, 2.516], so the ReLU never clips; through its 0.026 output weight it adds 0.026*1.02 = 0.026 per SD of restecg:2 to the logit (logit-term SD 0.026 vs total logit SD 4.3), i.e. it is practically inert and simply nudges the direct restecg:2 weight from 0.224 to 0.250. Closed-form err 0.0083 (3-s.f. rounding).
ann_29.proposed: This part barely changes the predictions.

ann_30.original: Hypothesis: serial composition H(G(sex:0, exang:0, restecg:2), slope:2). Node 3598 = relu(1.51 slope:2 + 1.05 G - 0.76) and node 1650 = relu(1.29 G + 1.31*3598 - 0.73). Because G takes only the values 0 or 2.117 and slope:2 is binary, 1650 has exactly four regimes on train: G=0 & slope not flat -> 0 (n=131, 27% positive); G=0 & flat slope (slope:2) -> 0.446 (n=103, 63% positive); G on & slope not flat -> 2.097 (n=1, negative); G on & flat slope -> 6.092 (n=7, all positive). So without the gate it is a small additional flat-ST-slope bonus (+0.34 logit after the 0.772 output weight, on top of the direct slope:2 weight); with the gate it amplifies the female-exertional-angina signal, and the flat-slope ReLU 3598 makes the two conditions super-additive (6.09 vs 0.45+2.10). Evidence: activation_profile on node 1650 (train): active 45.9%, mean 0.375, SD 1.018, max 6.092; values confirmed by local forward pass.
ann_30.proposed: A part that acts on patients with a flat ST segment and raises their risk, more so if exercise brings on chest pain.

ann_31.original: Hypothesis: additive composition. The logit z of node 0 is a linear score over 17 direct standardized inputs (dominated by ca 1.93, sex:1 1.67, cp:4 1.21, slope:2 1.05, chol 0.72, oldpeak 0.71) plus 0.772 x flat_slope_amplifier plus 0.026 x restecg2_relay; 7 inputs (trestbps, fbs:0, restecg:0, restecg:1, exang:1, thal:3, thal:4) are disconnected. get_formula shows node 0 as ReLU, but for this binary task the model output is sigmoid(z) on the pre-activation (compute_performance train AUC 0.945 equals AUC of z; sigmoid(relu(z)) would give 0.912). Evidence (train, n=242, local forward passes): direct-linear logit SD 4.33 vs amplifier term SD 0.79 vs relay term SD 0.026. Dropping the amplifier term lowers train AUC 0.945 -> 0.930 and accuracy 0.888 -> 0.868; the direct linear part alone gives AUC 0.931. So the network is essentially logistic regression plus one sparse nonlinear correction: a flat-slope bonus (+0.34 logit) and a large boost (+4.7 logit) for the 7 women with exertional angina, no LVH and flat ST slope. Kernel SHAP on the full model (train) ranks ca 0.149, sex:1 0.130, slope:2 0.121, cp:4 0.116, oldpeak 0.049, thal:7 0.046, chol 0.044 (mean |SHAP| on probability). Function preservation after the two input splits: max abs err 1.8e-15.
ann_31.proposed: More vessels coloured by fluoroscopy, a flat ST segment, higher cholesterol, more ST depression on exercise, a reversible thallium defect and older age raise the risk. Being a woman, typical or non-anginal chest pain rather than none and a higher maximum heart rate lower it. Resting blood pressure is ignored.

summary.text: The model's strongest signal is the number of major vessels coloured by fluoroscopy: from 0 to 2 vessels the odds of heart disease rise about 76 times on average, on the model's odds scale.
Women, and patients with typical angina or non-anginal chest pain rather than no chest pain symptoms, get a clearly lower risk.
A flat ST segment at peak exercise, higher cholesterol and more ST depression on exercise each clearly raise the risk.
Chest pain brought on by exercise raises the risk only if the resting ECG is normal.
One small part acts on just 8 training patients, all women whose chest pain is brought on by exercise, and raises their risk sharply; 7 of the 8 had heart disease.
The model ignores resting blood pressure.

worth_checking.text: Worth checking: the model ignores resting blood pressure entirely.
Worth checking: chest pain brought on by exercise has no effect on the risk of patients whose resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy.
Worth checking: the sharp rise in risk for women with chest pain brought on by exercise rests on 8 training patients.
Worth checking: the model treats a fixed defect on the thallium scan as lowering the risk compared with a normal scan, from only 15 training patients.
Worth checking: patients with typical angina get the lowest risk of all chest pain types, below patients with no chest pain symptoms.

outcome.positive: heart disease (more than 50% narrowing of a major coronary artery on angiography)

parts.name: female_exertional_angina_gate
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: node 665 is a three-way AND gate that fires only for women (sex:0 set) with exercise-induced angina (exang:0 unset, i.e. exang=yes) and no left-ventricular hypertrophy on resting ECG (restecg:2 unset). The restecg:2 chain 2349 -> 2771 never leaves the ReLU linear region on standardized one-hot inputs (2349 in [1.15,3.11], 2771 in [1.99,3.72]), so the gate collapses exactly to relu(1.41 sex:0 - 1.71 exang:0 - 1.18 restecg:2 - 3.39). Evidence (train, n=242): pre-activation max is 2.117, reached only when all three conditions hold; removing any one condition drives it negative (no female: -0.86; no exang: -2.53; LVH present: -0.24). The gate is active on 8/242 rows (3.3%), always at the single value 2.117, and 7 of those 8 are positive cases. Closed form matches the forward pass (check_explanation closed-form err 0.0049, numeric err 0).

parts.name: restecg2_relay_2447
parts.original_hypothesis: Hypothesis: node 2447 is an always-active affine relay of restecg:2 (LVH on resting ECG). Evidence (train): pre-activation in [0.485, 2.516], so the ReLU never clips; through its 0.026 output weight it adds 0.026*1.02 = 0.026 per SD of restecg:2 to the logit (logit-term SD 0.026 vs total logit SD 4.3), i.e. it is practically inert and simply nudges the direct restecg:2 weight from 0.224 to 0.250. Closed-form err 0.0083 (3-s.f. rounding).

ann_28.text: This part acts on 8 of 242 training patients (3%); nearly all of them are women and patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise.
For them it raises the risk of heart disease (odds about ×55 on average, on the model's odds scale). The model has little data on this: only 8 training patients (patients the part acts on).
In the training data, 7 of these 8 patients had heart disease.

The model gives women a lower risk than men, and even more so if exercise does not bring on chest pain (odds about ×0.03 for patients without chest pain on exercise against ×0.14 for patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise, on the model's odds scale).

The model gives women a lower risk than men, and even more so if the resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy (odds about ×0.03 for patients whose resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy against ×0.08 for patients with a normal resting ECG, on the model's odds scale).

The model gives patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise a higher risk than patients without chest pain on exercise, but only if the resting ECG is normal (odds about ×2.5 for patients with a normal resting ECG against ×1.00 for patients whose resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives women a higher risk through this part than men (odds about ×1.68 on average, on the model's odds scale).

The model clearly gives patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise a higher risk through this part than patients without chest pain on exercise (odds about ×1.62 on average, on the model's odds scale).

The model clearly gives patients whose resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy a lower risk through this part than patients with a normal resting ECG (odds about ×0.76 on average, on the model's odds scale).

ann_29.text: Through this part, the model also slightly raises the risk of heart disease with signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG (rather than a normal resting ECG).
This part barely changes the model's predictions (by at most 0.7 percentage points of risk).

ann_30.text: This part acts on 111 of 242 training patients (46%); nearly all of them are patients with a flat ST segment.
For them it clearly raises the risk of heart disease (odds about ×1.88 on average, on the model's odds scale).
In the training data, 72 of these 111 patients had heart disease.

The model gives patients with a flat ST segment a higher risk than patients with an upsloping ST segment, and even more so if exercise brings on chest pain (odds about ×18 for patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise against ×14 for patients without chest pain on exercise, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives women a higher risk through this part than men (odds about ×1.68 on average, on the model's odds scale).

The model clearly gives patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise a higher risk through this part than patients without chest pain on exercise (odds about ×1.62 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives patients with a flat ST segment a higher risk through this part than patients with an upsloping ST segment (odds about ×1.54 on average, on the model's odds scale).

The model clearly gives patients whose resting ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy a lower risk through this part than patients with a normal resting ECG (odds about ×0.76 on average, on the model's odds scale).

ann_31.text: The model clearly treats a higher number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy as raising the risk of heart disease: going from 0 vessels to 2 vessels changes the odds by about ×76 on average, on the model's odds scale.
The model clearly gives patients with typical angina a lower risk than patients with no chest pain symptoms (asymptomatic) (odds about ×0.04 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives women a lower risk than men (odds about ×0.05 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives patients with a flat ST segment a higher risk than patients with an upsloping ST segment (odds about ×15 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives patients with non-anginal chest pain a lower risk than patients with no chest pain symptoms (asymptomatic) (odds about ×0.07 on average, on the model's odds scale).

The model clearly treats a higher serum cholesterol as raising the risk of heart disease: going from 193 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L) to 308 mg/dL (8.0 mmol/L) changes the odds by about ×5.5 on average, on the model's odds scale.
The model clearly treats a higher ST depression on exercise as raising the risk of heart disease: going from 0.0 mm to 2.8 mm changes the odds by about ×5.3 on average, on the model's odds scale.

The model gives patients with a fixed defect on the thallium scan a lower risk than patients with a normal thallium scan (odds about ×0.29 on average, on the model's odds scale). The model has little data on this: only 15 training patients (a fixed defect on the thallium scan).
The model clearly gives patients with a reversible defect on the thallium scan a higher risk than patients with a normal thallium scan (odds about ×3.0 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly gives patients with atypical angina a lower risk than patients with no chest pain symptoms (asymptomatic) (odds about ×0.44 on average, on the model's odds scale).
The model clearly treats a higher age as raising the risk of heart disease: going from 42 years to 66 years changes the odds by about ×2.0 on average, on the model's odds scale.
The model clearly gives patients whose chest pain is brought on by exercise a higher risk than patients without chest pain on exercise (odds about ×1.62 on average, on the model's odds scale).

The model clearly treats a higher maximum heart rate as lowering the risk of heart disease: going from 118 beats per minute to 175 beats per minute changes the odds by about ×0.76 on average, on the model's odds scale.

The model also slightly raises the risk of heart disease with a downsloping ST segment (rather than an upsloping ST segment) and signs of left ventricular hypertrophy on the resting ECG (rather than a normal resting ECG); it slightly lowers it with fasting blood sugar above 120 mg/dL (rather than fasting blood sugar of 120 mg/dL or less).

For a typical patient (the median training patient for every number and the most common category for the rest; predicted risk 23%), the odds change, on the model's odds scale, by about number of vessels coloured by fluoroscopy from 0 vessels to 2 vessels: ×76; female rather than male: ×0.03; typical angina rather than no chest pain (asymptomatic): ×0.04; a flat ST segment rather than an upsloping ST segment: ×14; serum cholesterol from 193 mg/dL (5.0 mmol/L) to 308 mg/dL (8.0 mmol/L): ×5.5.
It ignores resting blood pressure.
